From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: SkylineBI onramp: private connectivity + SDK next steps

Calvin — great conversation earlier, thanks for the time. Quick written recap and suggested next steps so we have a single source of truth.

High-level goal
- SkylineBI wants a private onramp for inference traffic (embeddings + generation + rerank requests) with predictable latency and no public egress from your model clients.

Areas we covered and immediate asks
1) Networking & private connectivity
   - Preferred pattern: customer-managed VPC endpoint (AWS Interface Endpoint or PrivateLink) that routes to Redwood Private frontends in us-west-2. We can also support a regional transit option if you run across accounts.
   - Questions for you: can you attach a topology diagram showing where the app/pool runs, current NAT/egress points, and any transit gateways? Please attach if possible.

2) Auth & SDK setup
   - Two supported auth options for private onramp: mTLS (mutual TLS) with short-lived certs OR API key over a PrivateLink endpoint combined with IP allowlist. mTLS gives stronger identity guarantees; API-key is faster to prototype.
   - For mTLS we rotate client certs via your PKI or use Redwood-managed short-lived certs (we can support both). Do you have a preference?

3) Routing & DNS
   - We expect split-horizon DNS for the private endpoint (private A for endpoint) and a fallback public endpoint for hosted traffic. Confirm whether your infra supports split-horizon or conditional forwarding.

4) Structured outputs / tool calling / rerankers
   - These features (tool calls + structured output) work over the same private endpoint. If you plan to use embeddings + reranker pipelines, please share expected qps and token profile (average prompt length, average response tokens) so we can size dedicated capacity if needed.

5) Security/compliance evidence
   - You requested SOC 2 and data handling docs; attaching the standard onramp checklist (redwood-onramp-checklist.xlsx) for items we typically exchange. We can provide a short SOC2 evidence bundle during procurement.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
- Calvin: share the network sketch and expected qps/SAAS traffic profile (embedding vs generate) and preferred auth (mTLS vs API-key).
- Ben: can you prepare a short VPC endpoint options doc (1–2 pages) and a sample firewall rule set (ports/IPs) for Skyline?
- Lauren: please confirm commercial/contracting owner for Skyline; flag any special SLAs they need.

Proposed times for a technical deep-dive: Thu 2027-04-22 09:00 or Fri 2027-04-23 11:00 PT — call to include Calvin, Maria (infra), Ben, and me.

Thanks again — I’ll hold action items until we hear back.

Ben — can you own the technical design and reply with two recommended patterns by EOD:
  - Option A (recommended pilot): Interface Endpoint (PrivateLink) with API-key + IP allowlist. Fast to stand up; we can give a scoped API key and TTL. Include required firewall rules, expected egress IPs, DNS guidance (split-horizon), and whether embeddings/reranker traffic needs any special ports.
  - Option B (production/high-security): mTLS client certs with short-lived certs integrated with customer PKI (Vault). Outline the cert rotation flow, cert enrollment options (ACME vs SCEP vs Vault), and how we would validate at our ingress.

Also provide a minimal sample firewall rule set and the exact port/protocols (we generally use 443/tcp for TLS). If there are additional metadata endpoints (OCSP, CRL) they might need to allowlist, put those as well.

Lauren — confirm commercial owner and whether Skyline has an existing PO workflow (they flagged procurement/SOC2). I’ll add you to the call.

Thanks — looped in Calvin and Maria for transparency. High-level answers and attachments below; I’ll follow up with a short design doc by EOD.

Pilot (Option A) — Interface Endpoint + API key + IP allowlist- Pros: fastest to stand up, minimal infra changes, supports all features (embeddings/rerank/tool-calling) over TLS 443.- Cons: relies on API-key security, less strong identity than mTLS.

Recommended firewall / network rules (minimal)- Outbound from app to: <private-interface-endpoint-ip> (we will supply exact IP addresses once we provision)- Ports: 443/tcp (TLS for API + streaming)- DNS: use a private Route53 record (split-horizon) pointing api.private.redwood.example -> endpoint IPs- Egress: no public egress required if PrivateLink is used; if your app needs to reach public hosted model endpoints as fallback, allowlist our public egress range: 54.243.12.0/22, 3.14.25.0/24 (we will provide full CIDR list in final doc)

Production (Option B) — mTLS + short-lived certs- We can integrate with Vault PKI: the flow is client requests cert from Vault, Vault issues short-lived cert; customer registers public root with Redwood; our ingress validates client certs during TLS handshake.- Rotation: we recommend cert TTL < 24 hours for strong security; we support automated rotation via SCEP/ACME integrations or a simple cron-driven renew with Vault.- OCSP/CRL: allow outbound to our OCSP responder endpoints (ocsp.redwood.ai) if you opt for OCSP stapling/validation; otherwise CRL checking can be handled by the customer PKI.

Structured output & rerankers- No extra ports required — embedding and rerank requests are normal API calls over the private endpoint. If you plan to host large rerank batches, we recommend a small batching window on the client side and pinning a dedicated model variant (we can reserve capacity).

SDK notes- Our SDK supports both API-key and mTLS handshakes. For mTLS use the "client_cert" parameter in the SDK initializer and set the TLS context accordingly. Sample snippet included in attached mTLS-setup-steps.txt.

Action items and timeline- Ben (me): deliver 2-page VPC endpoint options + IP list + firewall rules by EOD Thu 2027-04-22.- Soojin: confirm contract owner with Lauren and share procurement contact.- Calvin/Maria: confirm preference (A or B) and confirm pilot schedule.

Attachments: redwood-vpc-endpoint-playbook.pdf, mTLS-setup-steps.txt

—
